proposals.evidence: Full *bōkka gives Prakrit bokkaḍa, Old Gujarati bokaḍaü, Gujarati bokṛũ, Marathi bokaḍ and Hindi bokrā “goat”. The selected survey forms retain this specific extended stem, with ordinary local gender/number endings and medial contraction or ḍ/ṛ variation; feminine i is analysed, not discarded as unexplained material. The CDIAL node includes these extensions. Turner’s tentative deeper origin and regional transmission remain unresolved.

proposals.evidence: Full bāhu gives Lahnda/Punjabi bā̃h, explicit Awankari bā̀ with plural bā̀vā̃, Kumaoni bā̃(h), and Western Pahari bā́/bái. The selected nasal, breathy and v/h forms fit this arm family, including contraction of intervocalic h and ordinary oblique/plural endings. Source breathiness/nasalization is retained. Forms with the z/j of bāzū and expanded -ṭ/-ṛ stems are excluded.
